title: D&D Sales over Time
unit: Estimated lifetime Player's Handbook copies sold, all channels, millions

editions.name: OD&D
editions.note: Tiny hobbyist print runs of the 1974 boxed set; no hard data found, so this is a rough guess.

editions.name: Basic D&D
editions.note: Not a PHB; this is all Basic sets combined. Ben Riggs' TSR figures, as quoted on ENWorld (secondhand), give about 3.0M for the Basic Set across its editions (Moldvay about 1.26M, Red Box about 1.1M, the rest Holmes and others). The 'tens of millions' claims online are unsourced. Riggs also has Basic at 500-700K/yr in the early 1980s, outselling the AD&D PHB+DMG combined for four years.

editions.name: AD&D 1e
editions.note: Riggs: PHB+DMG 'just above 750,000' combined in his TSR figures. Forum estimates put the PHB alone at 1.5M and a reader claims nearly 2M, both unsourced.

editions.name: AD&D 2e
editions.note: Ryan Dancey (via forums): TSR sold 289,000 2e PHBs in 1998 alone. A YouTuber estimate cited on ENWorld says 750K lifetime.

editions.name: 3e
editions.note: WotC: the three core books passed 1M combined within about two years (roughly 300K each); Dancey: 300K PHBs in the first 30 days. Acaeum estimate of 150-200K PHBs/yr across the 3e era.

editions.name: 3.5e
editions.note: Older recollection puts 3.5 at roughly 250-350K overall, but the 5e PHB sold 10x the 3.5 PHB in big-box channels alone, which implies hobby-store sales made up much of it.

editions.name: 4e
editions.note: WotC court filings say 'hundreds of thousands'. Forum guesses range from 200K to under 800K. WotC never released totals.

editions.name: 5e (2014)
editions.note: Floor: 1.56-1.6M PHBs through BookScan alone (US big-box/Amazon, mid-2023). BookScan is estimated at 23-34% to 85% of total depending on who you ask, so the true figure is higher; Teos Abadia's math implies 4.5-6M. Best guess is 4M for the 2014 book.

editions.name: 5.5e (2024)
editions.note: In progress, and WotC has published no unit counts. Anchors: a WotC exec said the English PHB sold in its first month what the 2014 PHB took nearly two years to sell across all languages. The 2014 PHB had BookScan sales of about 1.56M by 2023 (US only) and Mearls said it had outsold the lifetime PHBs of 3e+3.5e+4e at about two years, so roughly 1.5M+ in month one is implied if the claim is literal and counts digital and sell-in. Against that, BookScan saw only 3,773 US copies in launch week, but it misses most hobby stores. Hasbro called it the 'strongest-ever start for D&D books' (Q3 2025). Range is wide on purpose.
